speaker: james_burbage
text: God's body. Put the quire under your arm and step out of the snow. I am done pretending this rule is a walking stick.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A cloak is a bad hiding place for a rule. Say it at this door. Not inside.

speaker: james_burbage
text: The nearest door is this one. A hot gill. An oath before either of us drinks. By the mass, on the cup, and not on one of his books.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: On the gill. I will hear it. I will not carry it past this door.

speaker: james_burbage
text: The great stone hall. The Upper Frater. It can be had of its owner outright.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Outright is a large word for a Friday.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Six hundred pounds, come the spring, when the money's found. I mean to roof us against the winter and the Lord Mayor and Giles Allen together.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six fingers, then, and not shillings.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Not shillings. I am done holding up a hand and hoping the man opposite prays. Six hundred.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is a great deal of money.

speaker: james_burbage
text: It's a great deal of roof.

speaker: james_burbage
text: He has heard it every night for a month. Let him look. If he drinks, the oath is his, and he still has nothing he needs to say.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am looking at the lancets. Stone, and tall. That is all I am doing with them.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Keep the rest in your mouth. Allen's ground is still Allen's. I am not pulling a timber out of the Theatre to pay for a hall.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I did not ask you to pull anything down.

speaker: james_burbage
text: The lease runs. The hall is another man's stone. The money is not found. Come the spring, and not a day of it in a tiring-house before then.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not writing six hundred in a book. Not in mine. The printer is on the far side of his own door, and he is staying there.

speaker: james_burbage
text: God's body, keep him there. This doorway is the end of it. If I hear the sum in Shoreditch I shall know the mouth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You will not hear it from this one.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Say the sum once, so I know you heard money and not a dream.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Six hundred pounds. It is a great deal of money. It's a great deal of roof. I have said both, and I am done.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Then take the quire home. By the mass, I have stood in that hall. The rule has done what I brought it to do.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am going home to put the quire down. At two I am only a sharer at the door, and the door will hear nothing.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Keep it so. A tiring-house is no place to say six hundred.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The cup is empty. The book is empty of this. That is the oath, kept.
